title: Microwindow Release Cadence and Surge Thresholds - Jul 2026 (Draft)
content: Purpose:\nThis working draft captures a lightweight microwindow release cadence for small feature pushes and dependency updates, plus an explicit surge/traffic threshold matrix to decide pause/rollback boundaries. Target audience: on-call release engineers, deploy shepherds, and service owners.
body:
Context and motivation:
- We frequently have small releases (<5% traffic changes) that can be deployed rapidly but lack a clear microwindow cadence. This doc proposes a standard: short preflight, controlled microwindow (15–60 minutes), and an explicit surge threshold matrix so teams stop guessing when to abort.

Definitions:
- Microwindow: a short, focused release window intended for low-risk changes (config flips, minor traffic routing, safe feature flags). Typical duration: 15–60 minutes.
- Surge: an increase in error rate, latency, or queue depth relative to baseline that indicates potential regression.
- Pause threshold: signal level at which rollout is paused for investigation.
- Rollback threshold: signal level at which we immediately roll back and restore previous routing.

Preflight checklist (30–90 minutes before window):
- Confirm owner and emergency contact listed in the release ticket. (owner, backup on call)
- Confirm canary weight plan and step increments (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 10%).
- Verify smoke-test suite is green on staging with the exact release artifacts. Add noted flaky tests to ticket if present.
- Ensure observability dashboards preloaded (latency, p95/p99, 5xx, user-facing error rate, queue depth).
- Reserve a quiet channel in Slack: #releases-microwindow and add pager contacts.
- Validate alert routing and sampling settings (no new noisy alerts expected).
- Confirm fallback model variants or smaller quantized runtime available if needed.
- Double-check config flags and environment variables; lock unrelated feature flags for the microwindow.

Microwindow rollout plan (example 30-minute cadence):
- T0: Start window, announce in Slack with ticket link and expected increments.
- T0+2m: Deploy artifact to canary pool (1% traffic or single instance). Run smoke tests and quick synthetic queries.
- T0+6m: If no anomalies and metrics stable -> increase to 5%. Run short load probe for 2 minutes.
- T0+12m: If stable -> increase to 15% (or target steady-state if planned). Watch for 10–15 minutes.
- T0+25m: If all clears, promote to remainder off-peak capacity or schedule next larger rollout window.
- Abort immediately on any Rollback threshold breach.

Surge and signal thresholds (baseline = 30-minute pre-window average unless noted):
- Metric: user-facing error rate (5xx + classified service errors)
  - Pause threshold: +300% relative increase OR absolute >0.5%
  - Rollback threshold: +600% relative increase OR absolute >1.5%
- Metric: p95 latency for critical API
  - Pause threshold: +40% relative increase OR absolute increase >300ms
  - Rollback threshold: +80% relative increase OR absolute increase >700ms
- Metric: queue depth/backpressure on ingress
  - Pause threshold: sustained 2x baseline for 3 minutes
  - Rollback threshold: sustained 4x baseline for 1 minute
- Metric: downstream dependency error rate (DB, caches)
  - Pause threshold: any sustained error rate >2% for 5 minutes
  - Rollback threshold: sustained >5% or unbounded errors for 2 minutes

Notes on composite signals:
- If two pause-level signals fire within a 5-minute window, treat as rollback-level incident unless quick mitigation (feature flag off) resolves it.
- If a single noisy external monitoring anomaly (e.g., cloud provider API flapping) causes alerts but not user impact, coordinate with SRE and consider continuing with close monitoring.

Quick decision rubric for the release owner:
- Green path: no pause signals in first 12 minutes -> proceed with planned increments.
- Pause path: one pause signal -> stop increments, investigate for up to 10 minutes, attempt mitigation (revert config, reduce weight). If resolved -> continue cautiously, otherwise escalate and rollback.
- Immediate rollback: any rollback threshold breach or hard evidence of data corruption, privacy violation, or production crashes.

Rollback play (fast restore):
- Trigger: rollback threshold hit or escalation from service owner.
- Steps: revert traffic routing first, then revert deployment if routing revert insufficient. Post-rollback: capture snapshot of logs, traces, and JVM/process dumps and attach to ticket.
- Communication: immediate Slack banner in channel + page SRE lead, followed by short incident notes in ticket.

Telemetry and artifacts to collect during microwindow:
- A 10-minute rolling window of traces sampled at 50% for the canary cohort.
- Error logs with stack traces from the canary pool aggregated to ticket.
- p95/p99 heatmap and request histograms.
- Synthetic smoke test results (timestamped).

Post-window retrospective (within 48 hours):
- Owner to file short notes in ticket: timeline of steps, signals observed, mitigations, and final decision.
- If any pause/rollback occurred, include a 1-page root cause hypothesis and next step plan.
- Optional: add a short production replay on staging with identical traffic profile to reproduce.

Edge cases and special considerations:
- Data-migration changes: microwindow cadence NOT recommended. Use extended validation windows and schedule during low usage with database migration playbooks.
- Cross-region releases: apply independent microwindows per region, but coordinate global features that require synchronized cutovers.
- Model or embedding changes: include a quality-check step for downstream prediction drift; pause if automatic evaluation drops by >5% on the golden set.

Runbook snippets (copy-paste for ticket):
- Slack announcement template: "Starting microwindow for {{ticket}}. Owner: @owner. Canary 1% now. Watch p95 & error rate. Pause threshold: error +300% / p95 +40%. Link: {{dashboards}}"
- Rollback command template: "infra traffic-route revert --svc {{service}} --to baseline --auth=ops-key"

Open questions for follow-up:
- Should pause/rollback thresholds differ by team SLA tier? Proposal: keep core signals uniform but allow ± modifiers for Tier 1 enterprise customers.
- How to automatically compute baseline during highly seasonal days? Suggest using 24h rolling baseline with anomaly-smoothing.
- Should we add a canary-specific sampling level for traces during microwindows? Current default 50% may be too high for high-traffic services.

Action items (short):
- Rina to prototype a microwindow dashboard that surfaces the three composite signals with color-coded pause/rollback markers (ETA: 1 week).
- Marcus to add traffic-route revert command to the operations CLI with a one-line rollback alias (ETA: 3 days).
- Aisha to run two dry-run microwindows with release-lab group next week and capture signal fidelity.

Appendix: example ticket checklist (to paste at top of release ticket)
- [ ] Owner and backup listed
- [ ] Slack channel reserved
- [ ] Dashboards pinned
- [ ] Canary plan documented
- [ ] Preflight smoke tests green
- [ ] Rollback alias verified
- [ ] Observability sampling set

Developer notes (notes to self left intentionally rough):
- Keep microwindow lightweight. We lose velocity if every small change needs a multi-hour window. But we need solid stop conditions.
- Thresholds tuned conservatively for now; will relax after two weeks of green runs.
- Make sure the traffic-route revert is idempotent and quick across clusters.

Document history:
- 2026-07-12: initial draft by Aisha Patel
- 2026-07-15: added surge matrix and composite signal rules (Marcus Liu)
- 2026-07-18: clarified rollback play and action items (Rina Gomez)

End of draft.
